title: Plus One
description:
You are given a non-negative integer represented as an integer array `digits`, where each `digits[i]` is the `i`-th digit of the integer ordered from most significant to least significant (left to right). The integer contains no leading zeros except for the single-digit number `[0]` itself.

Increment the large integer by one and return the resulting array of digits. Note that the integer may be far larger than a 64-bit integer.
constraints: digits does not contain any leading 0's (except [0] itself).
hints: Simulate elementary-school addition starting from the least significant digit on the right.
If a digit is less than 9, increment it and immediately return — no further carry propagates.
If a digit is 9, set it to 0 and continue left; if every digit was 9, prepend a leading 1 to a new array of length n + 1.

examples.explanation: 9 + 1 = 10, which carries into a new leading digit to produce [1, 0].
